rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to capture all 10 compounds without truncation and map the overall elution window. The wide phi range and midrange slope should reveal whether retention is compressed, excessively long, or if early peaks are near-void.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only lever is time; shorten the gradient one step while keeping the same window and temperature to see how much resolution margin remains. This directly tests whether the current broad method can be accelerated without dropping any pair below 1.5.

Resolution is still complete at 16 min but the worst pair is already close to the 1.5 threshold, so take one more step shorter at the same conditions to find the time limit. If the critical pair stays above 1.5, this should improve CRF further; if not, we will know 16 min is near-optimal for this window.

The 14 min run became resolution-limited only at pair 6/7, while 16 min is fully resolved but slightly too slow, so raise temperature one step at tG 16 to try to pull the last peak below 10 min without sacrificing the critical pair. This is the cleanest way to gain time when slope is already near the resolution limit.

The critical pair 6/7 is not helped by higher temperature, so try changing the phi window instead: compressing the upper end should keep all peaks in-gradient while making the gradient shallower where most compounds elute. The observed elution window suggests the last peak is still well below phi 0.80, so this should preserve speed and may improve the selectivity/resolution of the crowded midsection.

Narrowing the gradient to phi1 0.80 restored full resolution but made the run a bit too long, so now shorten tG one step with the improved window. This tests whether the shallower effective slope around the crowded region gives enough margin to get t_last under 10 min while keeping pair 6/7 above 1.5.

At 12 min the run is already under 10 min but still limited only by pair 6/7, so slightly lowering phi1 should make the gradient shallower in the crowded elution region and may lift that pair above 1.5 with only a modest effect on the last peak. The previous shift from 0.95 to 0.80 improved the critical pair, so a smaller step in the same direction is the most promising refinement.

The 0.75 window nearly fixes the critical pair, so shorten tG one more step to pull the last peak back under 10 min and see whether pair 6/7 stays close enough to 1.5 for a net CRF gain. This probes whether the current window can beat injection 7 by trading a small amount of resolution for elimination of the time penalty.

Going from phi1 0.80 to 0.75 improved the critical pair much more than changing tG, so continue that trend and lower phi1 one more step while keeping tG 12. The last peak is still likely to remain near 10 min, and this is the best chance to push pair 6/7 to full credit or very close to it.

The first peak is still comfortably retained, so raising phi0 one step should trim dead time and slightly steepen the early part without changing the successful upper window too much. This may pull t_last just under 10 min while keeping the critical 6/7 pair near the strong resolution seen at phi1 0.75.

We have reached the maximum CRF, so now probe whether the method can be made still faster while keeping all pairs at or above 1.5; increasing phi0 one more step is the least disruptive way to trim retention. The first peak remains well beyond the void, and the current worst pair has a small but real margin.

A second increase in phi0 improved speed again without hurting the critical pair, so continue in the same direction to locate the highest feasible starting organic content. This should further shorten the method while monitoring whether the first peak approaches the void or pair 6/7 begins to deteriorate.

phi0 0.20 pushed the critical pair below full resolution credit, so revert to the best-resolved start and now shorten tG one step to see if we can keep pair 6/7 at or above 1.5 while gaining more speed. This is the natural boundary test around the fully successful 0.15/0.75/12 method.

The best fully successful region is around phi0 0.10–0.15, phi1 0.75, tG 12; since shortening tG fails, test a slightly wider upper window to see if pair 6/7 gains extra margin while still staying under 10 min. This checks whether 0.15/0.75/12 is truly the local optimum or if a small phi1 increase preserves full score with a more robust critical pair.

Since temperature at 45 C badly hurt selectivity, test one step lower than 40 C on the best 1.000 method to see if the critical 6/7 pair gains margin while staying under 10 min. This explores the remaining major variable around the optimum and could identify a more robust maximum-score condition.

We already have maximum CRF, so use the remaining budget to see whether phi0 0.15 can pair with a slightly lower phi1 to keep full resolution while still finishing under 10 min. This is the one nearby untested corner around the 1.000 methods that could preserve the score with a tighter, potentially more efficient gradient window.

The lower phi1 of 0.70 gives excellent resolution margin but slightly too much retention at phi0 0.15, so combine it with the better-balanced phi0 0.10 to see if the last peak drops under 10 min while preserving full resolution. This directly interpolates between the two 1.000 methods and the fully resolved 0.15/0.70 run.

We already have maximum CRF, so use this run to test robustness at the faster 0.15/0.75/12 composition by changing only temperature upward; if selectivity holds, this could reveal another 1.000 condition with more speed margin. The previous 45 C failure was at a different phi0/phi1 setting, so this combination is still worth checking once.

With the remaining nearby space, test whether the best 1.000 method can tolerate a slightly higher phi1 while keeping full resolution; this maps the upper boundary around the optimum and checks robustness of the critical pair. It also complements the already tested 0.15/0.80 condition by separating the effects of phi0 and phi1.

We already have the maximum score, so this run checks robustness on the shallow side of the proven optimum by lengthening tG one step at the best composition. If the critical pair gains substantial margin, it confirms 0.10/0.75/12 is very near the shortest fully resolved method and helps define the safe operating window.

With the optimum already found, use remaining injections to probe an alternate fast corner: the wider upper window may offset some of the resolution loss from a shorter 10 min gradient at phi0 0.15. This tests whether a different phi balance can achieve full or near-full resolution at a shorter gradient than the successful 12 min methods.

One of the two 1.000 methods remains untested at 45 C, and with only a small 1.58 margin on the critical pair this will confirm whether the temperature sensitivity is universally unfavorable or composition-dependent. It is the last informative single-variable check around the best method family.

A longer gradient at phi1 0.70 should strongly separate the critical mid-run pair while showing whether that tighter upper window can ever support a fully resolved method near the 10 min cutoff. This fills the last meaningful slope/window gap around the best family and may reveal an overlooked 1.000 alternative.

A slightly higher phi1 than the best method may trim the last-peak retention while testing whether the critical pair still stays above 1.5; this is one of the last nearby untried settings around the optimum. It helps bracket the upper-window boundary between the successful 0.75 method and the resolution loss seen at 0.80.

For the final run, test the remaining nearby corner around the two best methods: higher phi0 and higher phi1 together may keep the run short while revealing whether the 6/7 pair depends mainly on gradient window width or on absolute composition. This completes the local map around the 1.000 conditions without repeating any prior method.
